claims.statement: Revised EUDR application begins 30 December 2026 for large and medium operators and 30 June 2027 for most micro and small operators.
Operators placing covered commodities on the EU market must prove they are not linked to recent deforestation, and the Commission operates an information system for due-diligence statements.
Demand hypothesis: first placers will pay for a shipment gate, while simplified downstream obligations make downstream traders a poor initial segment.

contrary_evidence: The 2025 simplification reduced duties for downstream operators and traders.
Large importers and commodity platforms may already have traceability systems.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis: customs brokers and trade-finance providers embed the check across portfolios of importers
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 200 importers averaging 60000 PLN annual revenue could produce 12m PLN ARR; supplier continuity and broker distribution could yield founder equity above 5m PLN in 4-7 years
economics.founder_time: 18-24 hours weekly with forestry/legal expertise contracted per exception
economics.gross_margin_basis: Economics hypothesis: 68-84% because supplier exception handling is initially labour-heavy
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 12-18 months with fifteen importers and recurring shipment volume
economics.pricing: Economics hypothesis: 15000-50000 PLN onboarding, 2500-9000 PLN monthly and 50-200 PLN per shipment
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every shipment, new plot, new supplier and annual risk refresh

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Permissioned supplier-plot continuity, prior reference lineage and risk exceptions reduce marginal work on repeat shipments
fingerprint.customer: Polish medium and large first importers of timber, wood components and selected furniture inputs
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embedded in customs-broker, freight-forwarder and trade-finance document checklists
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Supplier evidence collection, geospatial preflight and authorised statement workflow sold as subscription plus shipment fee
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Importer pays per supplier onboarding and shipment released; broker may resell the service
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A covered purchase order approaches shipment before the first placer has complete geolocation and due-diligence evidence

founder_fit: Geospatial and supplier-data analysis suit data-science skills
Channel distribution avoids broad cold sales
risks: Supplier geolocation may be false or unobtainable.
Another legislative delay or simplification could weaken urgency.
Geospatial risk output must not be represented as a legal guarantee.

structure.control_point: Purchase-order or shipment release before the first EU market placement
structure.critical_dependency: Accurate upstream geolocation and lawful access to the EUDR Information System

thesis: A customs-broker- or trade-finance-embedded gate for wood and furniture inputs could prevent shipment release until the first EU placer has supplier legality evidence, plot geolocation, risk records and a due-diligence statement reference. The initial niche is Polish importers, not downstream firms relieved by simplification. Demand and economics are hypotheses.
title: EUDR First-Placer Purchase-Order Gate
uncertainties: Polish first-placer count in the chosen wood niche
Broker readiness to enforce a release gate
